Derived answer: the library IS drivable through Step 3 from current public API, so this measurement justifies no new facade or vocabulary. It also proves why the guide must not overclaim: lexical Jaccard exercises the end-to-end machinery but does not recover the manual targets for this precise paraphrase. Document it as a deterministic dependency-free baseline, with actual MAP anchors and support-bearing signature output, not as calibrated alignment quality. A quality claim needs a declared semantic provider and separate evidence.

Evidence scope: JVM consumer compile/run on Homebrew Java 25.0.1; no JS/Native, artifact publication, or site-build claim. No repository files touched.
